record.paper_title: Space and Time Complexity of Exact Algorithms: Some Open Problems
record.original_question: For the n-city travelling salesman path problem with cities 1 through n, a start at city 1, an end at city n, distances d(i, j), and the goal of visiting cities 2 through n-1 in some order while minimizing total path length, construct an exact algorithm running in O*(2^n) time while using only polynomial space, where O* suppresses polynomial factors.

evidence.quote: Construct an exact algorithm for the n-city TSP with O*(2n) time complexity and polynomial space complexity!

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let n ≥ 2 be an integer and let d : {1,…,n} × {1,…,n} → ℝ≥0 be a distance function. The (Hamiltonian path) travelling salesman problem asks for a permutation π of {2,…,n−1} that minimizes
  d(1, π(2)) + Σ_{i=2}^{n−2} d(π(i), π(i+1)) + d(π(n−1), n),
i.e. a minimum-length Hamiltonian path from city 1 to city n visiting every other city exactly once.

Design a deterministic exact algorithm that, on every such instance, computes the optimal value (and a corresponding optimal permutation) in time O*(2^n) while using only polynomial (in n) working space, where O*(·) suppresses factors polynomial in n and in the bit-length of the input distances. Equivalently: does there exist a 2^n · poly(n)-time, poly(n)-space exact algorithm for TSP?
artifact.status_search_result: Achieving an O*(2^n)-time polynomial-space exact algorithm for the general TSP is widely regarded as open. The classical Held–Karp algorithm achieves O*(2^n) time but uses exponential space, while known polynomial-space algorithms (e.g., Gurevich–Shelah, Bjorklund-type approaches) have worse running times such as O*(4^n · n^{log n}) or similar. Polynomial-space O*(2^n) algorithms are known only in restricted settings (bounded-degree graphs, many-visits TSP, etc.).

status_evidence.title: Approximating Asymmetric TSP in Exponential Time (Golovnev)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses Held–Karp O*(2^n) with exponential space and polynomial-space algorithms with worse time bounds; achieving O*(2^n) in polynomial space is a long-standing open question.
status_evidence.claim: O*(2^n) time with polynomial space for general TSP remains open.

status_evidence.title: A Polynomial-Space Exact Algorithm for TSP in Degree-6 Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Polynomial-space exact algorithms have been developed for bounded-degree TSP variants, indicating the general case is still unresolved.
status_evidence.claim: Progress exists only for restricted graph classes.

status_evidence.title: Space and time complexity of exact algorithms: Some open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Lists construction of an O*(2^n) time and polynomial-space exact TSP algorithm as an open problem.
